task_domain: web (Chinese-web browsing / agentic search) + multi-hop QA. A high-difficulty benchmark evaluating LLMs and agentic search systems on their ability to retrieve, filter, and reason over live information from the Chinese web to answer multi-constraint, multi-hop factual questions. Spans 11 topic domains (Film & TV, Technology, Art, History, Sports, Music, Geography, Policy & Law, Medicine, Video Games, Academic Research). It is a benchmark/evaluation paper, not a retrieval method.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent (or single-system) evaluation of web-browsing / information-seeking ability in Chinese, with no training/supervision provided to the evaluated systems (off-the-shelf evaluation of >20 SOTA systems). Each task is a reverse-engineered multi-hop question whose answer is a short, objective, easily verifiable fact (date, number, proper noun) with a unique answer. Three system categories are evaluated: (a) open-source LLMs and (b) closed-source APIs queried in direct-answer (often no web access) mode where they rely on internal knowledge, and (c) AI search products (agentic systems with live retrieval). For open/closed LLMs, decoding follows DeepSeek-R1 settings (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95) where configurable; for fixed-config models (O1, Claude-3.7) defaults are used; AI search products are exercised via human GUI interaction and their outputs recorded. Answers from open/closed models are extracted via regex and graded by GPT-4o using BrowseComp-style grading prompts; AI-search-product answers are manually extracted and verified by human annotators. Metrics are accuracy and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). The Chinese web (fragmented platforms such as Baidu Baike / Zhihu / government portals, inconsistent naming, censorship, implicit linguistic referents) is emphasized as a uniquely hard retrieval environment that English benchmarks (BrowseComp) and naive translations fail to capture.
what_is_retrieved: docs / live web content (for the web-enabled systems): search-engine results and web pages from the Chinese web (Baidu, Bing China, Google, and platform content such as Baidu Baike, Zhihu, government portals). For non-browsing LLMs, no external retrieval occurs; they answer from parametric knowledge. The benchmark itself does not prescribe a retrieval corpus - it measures whether a system can successfully retrieve and reconcile the supporting evidence chain for each reverse-designed question. Each ground-truth item also carries at least one authoritative source URL used during construction.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (the live open Chinese web / search engines) for the agentic-search systems; NOT an agent-written growing/episodic memory. Each question is anchored to verifiable web evidence (>=1 authoritative source URL collected at construction time). For pure LLMs evaluated without browsing, there is effectively no retrieval grounding (parametric-only). Overall the benchmark probes grounding against the open web rather than any persistent memory store.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a fixed top-k ranking nor a recall metric. The benchmark scores end-to-end answer ACCURACY (exact factual correctness of a unique short answer), so success implicitly requires recovering the COMPLETE evidence chain needed to satisfy all multi-hop constraints, but the paper reports no Recall@k / nDCG / completeness retrieval metric. Each question is constructed to have a single unique correct answer (answer-uniqueness validation), making it an outcome-completeness objective at the answer level rather than a candidate-list ranking objective.
retrieval_unit: document / web page + search result (for browsing systems): the unit a system must locate is the web evidence (page/snippet) that satisfies each constraint of a multi-hop question. There is no method-defined fine-grained retrieval unit (the paper is a benchmark, not a retriever); the de facto unit is whatever the evaluated system retrieves from search engines / web pages. The ground-truth answer unit is a short objective fact (date / number / proper noun, typically 5-10 Chinese characters).
index_source: Static, externally-defined: the live Chinese web accessed via three search engines (Baidu, Bing China, Google) for browsing systems; for non-browsing models, the model's frozen parametric knowledge. The benchmark dataset itself (289 questions) is offline, human-curated, and frozen; it is not induced from agent trajectories. Each item is grounded by >=1 authoritative source URL collected by annotators.
index_structure_topology: Not applicable as a method design. The retrievable surface is the unstructured, fragmented Chinese web (heterogeneous platforms: Baidu Baike, Zhihu, government portals, etc.) plus search-engine indexes; the paper highlights that this content is fragmented and inconsistently indexed (no single flat/graph/hierarchical index is imposed by the benchmark). The benchmark dataset is a flat list of 289 (question, unique-answer, source-URL, domain) records. [uncertain] beyond this, as no index structure is engineered by the authors.
retriever_type: Determined by each evaluated system, not by the benchmark. AI search products use their own proprietary retrieval/search pipelines (single-round retrieval: Kimi, Yuanbao/Hunyuan, DeepSeek; multi-round iterative retrieval: OpenAI DeepResearch, Perplexity Research, Doubao Deep Search). Pure LLMs use no retriever (LLM-as-parametric-knowledge). The benchmark is retriever-agnostic and treats systems as black boxes; it does not implement a BM25/dense/learned retriever of its own.
retriever_learning_signal: none from the benchmark (off-the-shelf). No retriever is trained by the authors; systems are evaluated as-is. Any learning signal lives inside the proprietary AI search products and is not controlled or specified by BrowseComp-ZH. The paper proposes (as future work) post-training such as reinforcement learning to improve browsing/reasoning, but does none itself.
query_construction: From the benchmark perspective, the query is the fixed reverse-designed natural-language Chinese question given to each system; systems then construct their own internal search queries from it. During DATASET CONSTRUCTION, annotators reverse-engineer each question from a known factual answer by combining multiple constraints (temporal, spatial, categorical, descriptive; >=2 dimensions typically), then test it on Baidu/Bing/Google with three distinct keyword combinations per engine to ensure non-trivial retrievability, and obfuscate lexical signals / add implicit constraints if GPT-4o and DeepSeek (web-enabled) solve it too easily.
query_granularity: task-level (one question per task, given once at t=0). The benchmark issues a single multi-hop question per item; how that decomposes into step/state-level sub-queries is left to each evaluated system (multi-round-retrieval products effectively perform trajectory/step-level sub-querying, single-round products do task-level retrieval). The benchmark does not prescribe query granularity.
when_to_retrieve: System-dependent, not prescribed by the benchmark. The analysis distinguishes single-retrieval systems (one round: Kimi, Yuanbao, DeepSeek) from iterative / multi-round-retrieval systems (DeepResearch, Perplexity, Doubao Deep Search), and shows multi-round (iterative/adaptive) retrieval yields substantially higher accuracy. Pure LLMs perform no retrieval (direct answer). The benchmark itself imposes no schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent/system-initiated and system-specific; the benchmark does not define a trigger. Multi-round systems decide when to re-search based on intermediate results (iterative refinement); single-round systems retrieve once; non-browsing LLMs never retrieve. No token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned-complexity-classifier, or reflection-token trigger is defined by BrowseComp-ZH. [uncertain] for the internal trigger logic of each proprietary product.
reranking: Not defined by the benchmark; any reranking happens inside the proprietary AI search products and is not specified or measured. No benchmark-level reranking stage exists.
retrieved_context_refinement: Not defined by the benchmark. The paper notes (qualitatively) that systems struggle to reconcile retrieved evidence with internal knowledge - e.g., enabling web search for DeepSeek-R1 DROPS accuracy from 23.2% to 7.6% because unreliable retrieved content overrides correct internal knowledge - implying weak/absent post-retrieval distillation/filtering in some systems. The benchmark itself applies no refinement; it measures the consequences of (in)adequate refinement in the evaluated systems.
how_retrieved_used: For browsing systems: prompt augmentation / answer synthesis - retrieved web evidence is used to produce a final short factual answer, requiring multi-hop reasoning and information reconciliation. For non-browsing LLMs: parametric-only answering. There is no training signal; usage is purely inference-time. The benchmark grades only the final extracted answer (plus a confidence estimate for calibration).
planning_integration: Not a method; the benchmark evaluates systems whose planning is internal. The key finding is that retrieve-then-reason pipelines with ITERATIVE (multi-round) retrieval (plan-search-refine loops, e.g., DeepResearch/Perplexity/Doubao Deep Search) substantially outperform single-shot retrieval and pure parametric answering on these multi-faceted queries. BrowseComp-ZH thus measures, rather than prescribes, planning-retrieval integration quality.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: System-dependent; not prescribed. Multi-round-retrieval products effectively interleave reasoning and search across multiple retrieval rounds (per-step / per-sub-query within a rollout), while single-round products do per-answer retrieval and pure LLMs do per-answer parametric reasoning. The benchmark grades per-answer outcomes only. [uncertain] for exact internal granularity of each product.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw web content / search snippets and pages (for browsing systems), surfaced in whatever form the proprietary product injects them; no distilled strategy, workflow, executable skill, or latent-token representation is defined by the benchmark. The benchmark's own stored items are plain-text Chinese question + short factual answer + authoritative source URL(s) + domain label.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Low abstraction: raw web documents / search results and concrete factual evidence (the literal answer is a single concrete fact such as a date, number, or proper noun). No distilled strategy, guideline, reusable workflow, or procedural skill is involved.
noise_robustness_mechanism: None built into the benchmark; robustness is instead MEASURED and shown to be a weakness. The paper documents that naively integrating retrieval without robust post-retrieval reasoning/alignment can HURT performance (DeepSeek-R1: 23.2% -> 7.6% when web search is enabled; calibration error also rises from 59% to 65%), attributing this to the model trusting less-reliable retrieved content over correct internal knowledge. Thus the benchmark exposes the absence of effective noise-robustness / evidence-reconciliation in current systems rather than providing a mechanism.
memory_type: none. BrowseComp-ZH is a static evaluation benchmark with no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory; evaluated systems are treated as black boxes and each question is answered independently.
write_back: false: the benchmark stores no new experiences/cases/skills; it is a frozen, human-curated test set. (Any internal memory of an evaluated product is out of scope and not measured.)
online_growth: false: the 289-question dataset is fixed and does not grow from agent outputs at test time. The dataset is released encrypted with a canary token to prevent pretraining contamination; the authors note future work to expand size/diversity (offline human curation, not online growth).
write_back_trigger: never: no memory write-back exists in the benchmark. Dataset items are created and validated entirely offline by human annotators through the two-stage quality-control protocol.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none: the benchmark does not store or retrieve failed experiences as memory. It performs qualitative analysis of failure modes (e.g., the DeepSeek-R1 search-degradation phenomenon, single-round vs multi-round retrieval gaps), and proposes future failure-case studies, but persists no negative cases for retrieval or learning.
memory_evolution_update: N/A: there is no model-written memory to mutate. The benchmark set is updated only by human curation; the authors note answers may drift over time given the dynamic web (a reproducibility caveat), but no automatic append/dedup/refine/forget mechanism exists.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: the benchmark does not learn or optimize any retrieval policy; it evaluates fixed off-the-shelf systems. No M-MDP / soft Q-learning / RL retrieval is involved (RL is mentioned only as future work to improve browsing/reasoning).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No shared memory across agents. Each system is evaluated independently and in isolation; there is no cross-agent or cross-framework experience/memory sharing. The benchmark does, however, enable cross-SYSTEM comparison (open-source LLMs vs closed-source APIs vs agentic search products) over the same task set.
benchmarks: BrowseComp-ZH (introduced by this paper): 289 reverse-engineered multi-hop Chinese questions across 11 topic domains, each with a short unique verifiable answer and >=1 authoritative source URL. Topic distribution (approx.): Film & TV 15.6%, Art 13.8%, Geography 12.8%, Music 11.1%, History 10.0%, Medicine 9.0%, plus Technology, Sports, Video Games, Policy & Law (3.5%), and Academic Research/Papers (2.4%). Question length mostly 60-90 characters; answer length mostly 5-10 characters. Inspired by and contrasted with the English BrowseComp (Wei et al., 2025).
benchmark_family: web (Chinese-web browsing / agentic search), closely paralleling BrowseComp; also a multi-hop knowledge-intensive QA benchmark. Positioned within the web-browsing/agent evaluation family alongside BrowseComp (English), GAIA, and the QA/multi-hop lineage (TriviaQA, HotpotQA, FEVER, KILT). Distinct from prior Chinese retrieval benchmarks (Level-Navi Agent, Chinese dynamic QA, CRUD-RAG, medical QA datasets CMExam / Huatuo-26M).
baselines: 23 evaluated systems in three categories. Open-source LLMs: DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, Qwen3-235B-A22B (Non-Thinking and Thinking), QwQ-32B, LlaMa4 (Maverick-instruct-basic). Closed-source APIs: GPT-4o, O1, O4-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Claude-3.7-Sonnet (20250219), Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro (preview-03-25), Qwen2.5-MAX. AI search products: OpenAI DeepResearch, Grok-3 (Research), Perplexity (Research), Doubao (Deep Search and Standard), Kimi (Deep Think), Yuanbao (Hunyuan), DeepSeek (Deep Think and Standard). Reasoning-vs-non-reasoning pairs (DeepSeek-V3 vs R1; Claude-3.5 vs 3.7; Gemini-2.0-Flash vs 2.5-Pro) serve as internal comparisons.
key_metrics: (1) Accuracy (%): fraction of questions answered with the correct unique short fact, graded by GPT-4o (BrowseComp-style prompt) for open/closed models and by human verification for AI search products. (2) Calibration Error - Expected Calibration Error (ECE, %): weighted average over 5 confidence bins ([0-0.2),[0.2-0.4),[0.4-0.6),[0.6-0.8),[0.8-1.0]) of |accuracy - confidence|, requiring models to emit confidence estimates. No Recall@k/nDCG, latency, or dollar-cost metrics are reported.
headline_result: Even the best system, OpenAI's DeepResearch, reaches only 42.9% accuracy (with the lowest calibration error, 9%). Most systems perform far worse: many below 10% (e.g., LlaMa4 4.8%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 5.5%, GPT-4o 6.2%, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct 6.6%), and only a handful exceed 20% (O1 29.1%, Gemini-2.5-Pro 27.3%, Doubao Deep Search 26.0%, DeepSeek-R1 23.2%, Perplexity Research 22.6%). The low ceiling (<43%) is the central difficulty signal.
ablations: (1) Reasoning vs non-reasoning (Sec 4.5): reasoning-augmented models consistently improve - DeepSeek-R1 23.2% vs DeepSeek-V3 8.7% (+14.5pp); Claude-3.7-Sonnet 17.7% vs Claude-3.5-Sonnet 5.5% (+12.2pp); Gemini-2.5-Pro 27.3% vs Gemini-2.0-Flash 6.9%; Doubao Deep Search 26.0% vs Standard 18.7% (~+8pp). (2) Single-round vs multi-round retrieval (Sec 4.6): multi-round/iterative systems (DeepResearch 42.9%, Doubao Deep Search 26.0%, Perplexity 22.6%) far exceed single-round ones (Yuanbao 12.2%, Kimi 8.0%, DeepSeek 7.6%); DeepSeek's deep-think search shows little gain because it does only a single retrieval round. (3) Counterintuitive retrieval harm: enabling web search for DeepSeek-R1 drops accuracy 23.2% -> 7.6% and raises ECE 59% -> 65%, indicating unreliable retrieved content overriding correct internal knowledge. (4) Calibration (Sec 4.7): adding search generally increases calibration error; DeepResearch is notably well-calibrated (ECE 9%).
evaluation_decoupling: No. The benchmark reports only end-to-end answer accuracy (plus calibration error); it does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG/retrieval completeness) decoupled from task accuracy. Retrieval quality is inferred indirectly via system-category comparisons (browsing vs non-browsing, single- vs multi-round) rather than measured standalone.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (final answer accuracy). The only additional axis is Expected Calibration Error (alignment of stated confidence with correctness), which is a meta-outcome rather than a process-quality metric. No step-wise retrieval/reasoning faithfulness or trajectory-quality scoring is reported; failure modes are examined qualitatively, and detailed process/failure analysis is deferred to future work.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified in dollar/latency/token terms. The paper qualitatively links higher accuracy to more expensive test-time compute - multi-round (iterative) retrieval and explicit reasoning improve accuracy ('test-time scaling through iterative retrieval'), while single-round retrieval is cheaper but markedly weaker. No explicit retrieval-call counts, API cost, latency, or token-budget tables are provided.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Not specified by the benchmark. No fixed token budget or fixed-k retrieval count is imposed; the number of retrieval rounds and amount of injected context are determined by each evaluated system (single-round vs multi-round). For open/closed LLMs, decoding follows DeepSeek-R1 settings (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95) where configurable; AI search products are run via their native GUIs.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Size: 289 validated questions across 11 domains, distilled from 480 preliminary samples. Construction: REVERSE-ENGINEERED by 10 expert annotators (Master's/PhD, with LLM and topical expertise) - start from a single objective verifiable answer (date/number/proper noun), craft a multi-constraint (>=2 dimensions: temporal/spatial/categorical/descriptive) Chinese question, verify non-trivial retrievability on Baidu/Bing/Google (rejected if the answer appears on any engine's first page using 3 keyword combos per engine), and obfuscate if GPT-4o + DeepSeek (web-enabled) solve it too easily. Two-stage quality control: Stage 1 difficulty validation - peer cross-checking using search engines only (no LLMs) under a strict 10-minute limit, removing 76 easy samples (404 remain); Stage 2 answer-uniqueness validation - top systems (OpenAI DeepSearch, Perplexity, Doubao deep-reasoning, OpenAI O1, Gemini-2.5-Pro) generate candidate answers, annotators reject any question for which an alternative answer also satisfies all constraints, removing 115 ambiguous samples (289 remain). Answer verifiability: HIGH - short, objective, unique answers grounded by >=1 authoritative source URL; graded by GPT-4o (BrowseComp prompt) for LLMs and human-verified for AI search products. Dataset released ENCRYPTED with a canary token to prevent pretraining contamination. Difficulty signal: best system (DeepResearch) only 42.9%; most systems <10%.
builds_on: BrowseComp (Wei et al., 2025, arXiv:2504.12516) - directly adopts its reverse-design philosophy, multi-constraint hard-to-retrieve / easy-to-verify question format, grading prompts (GPT-4o grader), and calibration-error methodology, extending it to the Chinese web. Conceptually builds on web-browsing/tool-use agent work (WebGPT, Toolformer, ReAct), RAG (Guu et al. 2020; Lewis et al. 2020), and the multi-hop / knowledge-intensive QA lineage (TriviaQA, HotpotQA, FEVER, KILT, GAIA).
contrasts_with: (1) English BrowseComp (Wei et al., 2025) - argues direct translation fails (structural/idiomatic mismatch, missing Chinese equivalents of Wikipedia/IMDb, queries collapsing into keyword matches), motivating native Chinese construction. (2) Prior Chinese retrieval/QA benchmarks shown to be insufficient: Level-Navi Agent (Hu et al., 2024, lacks difficulty/accessibility control), Chinese dynamic QA (Xu et al., 2024, no multi-hop emphasis), CRUD-RAG (Lyu et al., 2025, generation-quality focus over retrieval-path validation), and medical-domain QA (CMExam / Huatuo-26M, domain-specific, no open-ended browsing). (3) Keyword-retrievable classic QA benchmarks (TriviaQA/HotpotQA/FEVER/KILT/GAIA) that fail to test complex search-trajectory planning.
lineage: Surveys/Benchmarks group: a benchmark (not a method) in the web-browsing / agentic-search evaluation lineage. It is the Chinese-web counterpart of BrowseComp (English), extending reverse-engineered, evidence-grounded, hard-to-retrieve / easy-to-verify multi-hop question design into the fragmented Chinese information ecosystem, and serves as a difficulty-defining testbed (best system 42.9%) for diagnosing the retrieval-plus-reasoning and evidence-reconciliation limits of contemporary LLMs and AI search products.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: no, Reuse: no, Revise: no, Retain: no] - not a case-based-reasoning system; it is an evaluation benchmark.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. (It does cite CBR-RAG (Wiratunga et al., 2024) once in Related Work as an example RAG-for-QA application, but BrowseComp-ZH itself is not a CBR method.)
tool_document_engineering: N/A: not a tool-retrieval method; no tool/skill descriptions are processed or indexed.
index_content_separation: N/A: no lightweight-index-then-content design; the benchmark dataset is a flat record set and the retrievable surface is the open Chinese web.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A: the benchmark does not define a tool index or integration protocol. Browsing systems use their own search-engine / web access; the benchmark notes the live web's temporal volatility as a reproducibility caveat.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A: no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use benchmark in the function-calling sense (it is a web-browsing / search benchmark).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not framed as CBR; no retrieved-case adaptation).
